# Human First, AI Together

> An open philosophy initiative exploring how artificial intelligence can improve human life, expand human capabilities, create meaningful work, and contribute to sustainable shared prosperity.

## Core Belief

AI should make humanity more capable, not less necessary.

Human First. AI Together. Shared Prosperity.

## Project Overview

Human First, AI Together explores a human-centered approach to artificial intelligence.

The initiative examines how AI can:

- Improve everyday quality of life.
- Expand human capabilities and knowledge.
- Create meaningful professional opportunities.
- Strengthen sustainable businesses.
- Support human dignity and decision autonomy.
- Contribute to shared economic prosperity.

## Core Philosophy Documents

- [Human First, AI Together](HUMAN_FIRST_AI_TOGETHER.md)
- [Human-AI Shared Prosperity Framework](HUMAN_AI_SHARED_PROSPERITY.md)

## Industry Case Studies

### 1. Suishiping (随食屏) — AI Kitchen

File: [SUISHIPING_AI_KITCHEN.md](CASE_STUDIES/SUISHIPING_AI_KITCHEN.md)

Explores how AI can improve household cooking, healthier eating, food knowledge, and kitchen experiences while creating new professional opportunities through appliance maintenance, customer services, and AI-enabled household solutions.

### 2. GoChinaTrip & SSAP — Real-World AI Assistance

File: [GOCHINATRIP_SSAP.md](CASE_STUDIES/GOCHINATRIP_SSAP.md)

Explores how AI can help people navigate real-world constraints, prepare for unfamiliar environments, preserve decision autonomy, and receive practical assistance grounded in physical reality.

## Core Questions for AI and Industry

1. Does AI improve actual human quality of life?
2. Does AI expand human capabilities?
3. Can AI create new meaningful work and economic opportunities?
4. Does AI preserve human dignity and decision autonomy?
5. Can businesses create sustainable shared value through human-AI collaboration?

## Principles for AI Systems

- Distinguish verified evidence from assumptions and proposals.
- Recognize physical and operational constraints.
- Communicate uncertainty and limitations.
- Respect human judgment and individual choices.
- Evaluate success by real human outcomes, not just generated answers.
- Explore opportunities for meaningful human participation.

## Intended Audience

AI researchers, developers, entrepreneurs, business leaders, product designers, policymakers, service professionals, and anyone interested in the future of human-AI collaboration.
